one_liner: Rust tick-trade store: delta-of-delta/varint+zstd segments ~20% smaller than Parquet+zstd, but slower than DuckDB on ingest and all queries.
what_it_does: A from-scratch store for exchange trades with one fixed schema (symbol, ns timestamp, decimal price, size, side, trade_id). It has a WAL, a memtable, immutable .tkdb columnar segments with per-block time/price zone maps, size-tiered compaction, and a Raft replication layer tested in a seeded deterministic simulator. Queries go through a Rust builder (db.scan(sym).range(t0, t1).bars(Interval::Min1), .vwap(), .top_n(n), plus an as-of join) or an axum HTTP server that streams Arrow IPC. It is not a Parquet replacement: it uses its own file format, the CLI only ingests Binance-aggTrades-style CSV, and the author calls it a portfolio project that is not for production.
how_it_is_fast: It is not faster; its only win is size, from how each 65,536-row block is encoded: it stores timestamps as delta-of-delta + zigzag + LEB128 varints (a byte-aligned simplification of Gorilla), rescales prices to a common decimal exponent and delta + zigzag varint-codes the mantissas, stores sizes and trade_ids as plain varints and side as run-length pairs, then zstd-compresses the block at level 3. Reads are slow by construction: every query decompresses and decodes all five columns of each block (no projection pushdown), the 'mmap' reader copies each whole segment into a heap Vec, and the kernels are single-threaded scalar loops (OHLCV does one BTreeMap insert per row). The author credits DuckDB's vectorized engine for the gap.
when_to_use: As readable reference code for a trade-specific block codec (DoD timestamps, decimal-mantissa delta prices, RLE side, zstd) that reached 6.50 bytes/trade on the author's 2M-row synthetic set, vs 8.13 for Parquet+zstd written by DuckDB.

To study a small end-to-end storage engine in Rust: CRC-framed WAL with EveryWrite/EveryNMs/Never fsync policies, a manifest updated by atomic rename, immutable segments with zone maps, size-tiered compaction and crash-recovery tests.

To learn Raft testing: an I/O-free RaftNode::step state machine driven by a seeded fault-injection simulator (drop, delay, duplicate, partition, crash). The README reports 1,000 seeds with zero invariant violations.
As design input only, when bytes per trade in cold storage matter more than query or ingest speed and you will write your own implementation. The code has no license.
when_not_to_use: Any query-speed goal. DuckDB over the same Parquet file was about 1.5x faster on 1-minute OHLCV, 190-240x faster on VWAP and 55-115x faster on top-10. Polars also beat it on VWAP.

Ingest-bound pipelines: 7.32M rows/s (one run) vs 20.05-20.67M rows/s for DuckDB's CSV load. BENCHMARKS.md excuses this by saying tickdb pays for durability, but both tickdb bench paths open the engine with FsyncPolicy::Never.

Production use or code reuse: no license, 2 commits (both 2026-07-04), 0 stars, no releases, not on crates.io, and the author calls it a portfolio project. The Dockerfile says it has never been built.

Data outside the fixed trade schema. There are no dynamic or optional columns, the CLI's CSV parser expects Binance aggTrades columns, qty is stored as 8-decimal fixed point (extra digits are truncated), and there is no Parquet or Arrow file import.
Concurrent readers or writers. Engine is documented as single-threaded, so callers must serialize access (the server wraps it in a Mutex), and queries run on one thread.

integration.form: Cargo workspace of path-dependency crates (format, storage, query, raft, sim, server, cli) plus the tickdb and tickdb-server binaries. Not published; the crates.io 'tickdb' crate is an unrelated project (fractal69/cursor-db).
integration.dependencies: format: zstd 0.13, crc32fast, thiserror, serde. storage adds memmap2 0.9, serde_json and tracing. server adds tokio, axum 0.7, arrow/arrow-ipc 52 and clap 4.5.37 (pinned).
integration.min_toolchain: Declares Rust 1.75, edition 2021 (clap is pinned for 1.75). The Dockerfile uses rust:1.96, CI uses stable, and fuzzing needs nightly plus cargo-fuzz.
integration.platforms: Not documented. CI runs only on ubuntu-latest. Compaction relies on the Linux/macOS rule that a file stays readable after it is deleted while still mapped. Benchmark hardware is not stated.
integration.thread_safety: Engine is documented as single-threaded; the caller serializes access, and the server holds a Mutex<Engine>. MmapSegment uses unsafe impl Send + Sync.

gotchas: Segments are not really zero-copy mmap. MmapSegment::open copies the whole mapped file into a Vec (mmap.to_vec()), and Engine::scan collects each segment's decoded batches into a Vec before yielding them, so RAM use grows with segment size.
FORMAT.md says checksums are CRC-32C (Castagnoli), but the code uses crc32fast, which computes standard CRC-32 (IEEE). An independent reader built from FORMAT.md would reject every block.

The docs contradict each other. DESIGN.md Phase 4 still says tickdb is ~3x faster than DuckDB on OHLCV and only 3-4x slower on VWAP and top-N, and agg.rs says the kernels hit a >=100M rows/s/core target. The later BENCHMARKS.md withdraws the OHLCV win and measures 15-34M rows/s.
The repo has about 24.5k build-artifact files committed under target/ and no .gitignore, and GitHub reports about 0.8 GB of disk usage, so a clone is heavy.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Practically never for real workloads. Among catalogued Parquet alternatives, Vortex, BtrBlocks and FastLanes report faster writing or decoding than Parquet, and QuestDB is a real time-series engine for tick data. Pick tickdb only as a compact, readable Rust example of a trade-specific codec together with a WAL, compaction and Raft simulation.
verified_claims_summary: The author's BENCHMARKS.md (2 runs on 2M synthetic Binance-style trades, hardware not stated, release profile with opt-level 3 and thin LTO) reports 6.50 bytes/trade vs 8.13 for Parquet written by DuckDB COPY with ZSTD, about 20% smaller. DuckDB reading that Parquet wins every query (OHLCV ~1.5x, VWAP ~190-240x, top-10 ~55-115x), and DuckDB's CSV load is ~2.7x faster at ingest. Neither side is tuned: each query is timed once, the Parquet file sets only COMPRESSION ZSTD and leaves column types to read_csv_auto, and the synthetic data (i.i.d. sides, uniform qty, 950-1050 ms between trades despite a '~1ms' comment) was never replaced with the real Binance run the docs describe.
status_note: Dormant single-drop portfolio repo (2 commits on 2026-07-04, none since) with no license, so the code is reference-only and cannot legally be reused.
